title: Standardizing Research Operations at Scale
subtitle: A systemic overhaul of how a Fortune 50 fintech organization conducts, stores, and distributes UX intelligence across seven autonomous business units.
imageCaption: Cross-functional alignment workshop — Q1 2024, New York
challengeHeading: A knowledge infrastructure failing at scale
challengeBody: The client's UX research function had grown organically over seven years — each business unit developing its own tools, rituals, and repositories. What began as nimble autonomy had calcified into organizational debt: a fragmented ecosystem where valuable intelligence was siloed, duplicated, or simply lost.

Our mandate was to architect a unified research operations system — one that could serve a team of 40 active researchers while remaining legible to the 300+ non-researcher stakeholders who needed to consume, commission, and act on findings.
deliverablesDesc: All outputs were designed for longevity — built to evolve with the organization rather than expire with the engagement.

painPoints.text: Research artifacts scattered across 12+ disconnected repositories and storage systems.
No standardized recruitment pipeline — each study required rebuilding from scratch.
Duplicate studies conducted unknowingly across business units, wasting 30% of research budget.
Zero discoverability: findings had an effective shelf-life of 90 days before becoming inaccessible.
Average study lead-time of 11 weeks from inception to stakeholder briefing.

approach.desc: Comprehensive inventory of all existing research outputs, tools, and workflows across 7 business units.
approach.title: Landscape Audit

approach.desc: Designed a centralized taxonomy and metadata schema to make all research cross-searchable and retrievable.
approach.title: System Architecture

approach.desc: Co-created standardized recruitment protocols and study templates with embedded compliance guardrails.
approach.title: Process Design

approach.desc: Delivered a 3-module training programme enabling 60+ non-researcher stakeholders to access and interpret findings.
approach.title: Capability Building

findings.body: The primary failure mode was not a lack of research, but an inability to surface existing knowledge at the moment of need.
findings.title: Knowledge Fragmentation

findings.body: An average of 6.3 discrete tools were used per study with no enforced handoff — each transition was a data loss event.
findings.title: Tool Proliferation

findings.body: Research access was controlled informally by individuals rather than policy, creating bottlenecks and knowledge hoarding.
findings.title: Invisible Gatekeeping

findings.body: Without a tagging standard, 73% of archived studies were effectively unsearchable within 6 months of completion.
findings.title: Signal vs. Noise

deliverables.text: Standardized Study Brief and Protocol Templates
Recruitment Pipeline Design and Vendor SLAs
Executive Briefing: ROI of Research Infrastructure

outcomes.label: Research budget recovered
outcomes.sub: By eliminating duplicate studies across BUs

outcomes.label: Studies migrated and tagged
outcomes.sub: Fully searchable within 30 days of launch
